findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to child 4cc4 (or name the owning sibling) a test that pin-currency checks accept the engine-stamped agentic attestation identically to a pipeline one.
evidence: Parent Invariants: 'A non-blocking agentic PASS mints the same plan-review attestation, accepted identically by the claim and close gates, `rebar review-plan --status`, `sign-review`, and pin-currency checks.'
Child 4cc4 ACs: 'accepted by claim, close, `review-plan --status` and `sign-review`' — pin-currency absent.
4cc4 Scope does not list any pin-currency module or test.
findings.finding: The parent's 'Same certification' invariant names pin-currency checks as a consumer that must accept the agentic attestation identically, but no sibling's acceptance criteria exercise pin-currency against an agentic/engine-stamped attestation. Child 4cc4's ACs verify claim, close, review-plan --status and sign-review only; AC6 of the parent likewise omits pin-currency. No other sibling covers it.
scenarios: An agentic attestation with engine:"agentic" (or the missing-field pipeline default) passes a pin-currency check differently from a pipeline one, breaking a plan whose pin currency is re-validated after review.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend 4cc4's acceptance criteria to include pin-currency acceptance of the engine-stamped (and missing-field back-compat) attestation.

evidence: Parent AC-2: '...the provider-parity and prompt evals pass on the new models.'
Child 81a1 AC: 'The before (4.x) and after (5.5) prompt-eval summaries are recorded in a ticket comment, one line per spec with pass/fail and coverage.' — records pass/fail, does not require pass.
Child 7341 AC pins only 'The 5.5 provider-parity run reports invalid: false for both slots' — not prompt evals.
findings.finding: Parent AC-2 requires the provider-parity AND prompt evals to 'pass on the new models'. The prompt-eval half is delivered by child 81a1, but 81a1's binding acceptance criteria only require the before/after prompt-eval SUMMARIES to be recorded in a ticket comment (one line per spec with pass/fail and coverage); no sibling AC asserts that the 5.5 prompt-eval runs actually PASS. Child 7341 pins 'invalid: false' for provider-parity but is silent on prompt evals, and 81a1 records fail outcomes without requiring success.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend child 81a1's AC to require each after-run spec to meet its pass/coverage bar (or file any regression as a linked bug), matching the parent's 'prompt evals pass' wording.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, for the agentic engine's Bedrock-first+Anthropic-fallback chain, which disposition wins on fallback-failure — that the chain preserves the most-recoverable leg so a retryable Bedrock throttle (exit-11 / WAIT_AND_RETRY) is never masked by the fallback's own non-retryable failure before mapping to INDETERMINATE.
evidence: 'runs on rebar's existing LLM runtime and provider chain, so Bedrock-first with fallback still applies' — a secondary/fallback arm is present
'An agentic run that does not finish cleanly ... resolves INDETERMINATE through the same resolution_class path a failed pipeline pass uses' — collapses all non-clean outcomes to INDETERMINATE

ABSENCE: the plan never states, for the agentic engine's provider chain, which disposition wins when the fallback leg fails — the clause-2 / 1c0d concern that a retryable primary throttle must not be masked by the fallback's own non-retryable failure
findings.finding: The agentic engine reuses rebar's Bedrock-first provider chain with Anthropic fallback, but the 'Fail closed' invariant maps every non-clean outcome to INDETERMINATE without stating which disposition wins when the fallback arm itself fails — risking a retryable Bedrock throttle (exit-11 / WAIT_AND_RETRY) being masked by the fallback's own non-retryable failure and surfacing as INDETERMINATE.
findings.location: Invariants > 'Fail closed'; Approach item 3 ('Bedrock-first with fallback still applies')
scenarios: Bedrock returns a 429 (retryable); the Anthropic fallback's own auth/config fails (non-retryable); the agentic run reports INDETERMINATE instead of preserving the retryable WAIT_AND_RETRY disposition, so a transient throttle is treated as a terminal review outcome
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'Fail closed' invariant, add that the agentic engine's resolution_class path preserves the most-recoverable leg: a retryable primary failure (e.g. Bedrock 429 -> WAIT_AND_RETRY / exit-11) stays retryable even when the Anthropic fallback's own non-retryable failure occurs; only a genuinely terminal (non-retryable on every leg) outcome collapses to INDETERMINATE.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the model-upgrade step to add new-id rows for the 5.5 Bedrock/direct ids to `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` (temperature, native-output-under-thinking) and `_MODEL_CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`, so the audited API deltas are honored in the capability layer rather than only recorded.
evidence: capabilities.py:233-238 records `supports_temperature: False` for `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-4-7` and their `us.`/`global.` Bedrock ids specifically to avoid 'both its warning and a false claim that verifier decoding is pinned'
capabilities.py:284-287: a model id with no override row 'applies no override, leaving the profile/_REBAR_OVERRIDES-derived record as-is' — i.e. default `supports_temperature: True`

The audit in Approach step 2 names 'temperature, top_p and top_k are rejected' on the new models but step 2 only lists updating rebar.toml/bedrock.toml, MODEL_WINDOW_LADDER and the sizing ladder — not these capability tables
capabilities.py:38-54 keys cache minimums per-id; bare `claude-opus-5` has a 512 row but the plan's Bedrock ids (`us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`) would fall through to the 4096 fallback
findings.finding: The model-upgrade step audits the new models' API changes (temperature/top_p/top_k rejected, thinking always-on on Opus 5.5) but does not direct adding the corresponding new model-id rows to the existing per-id capability-override tables (`_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` and `_MODEL_CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` in capabilities.py). Without those rows the new Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 5.5 ids inherit family defaults (`supports_temperature: True`, no cache-min entry), re-introducing precisely the warning and false temperature-pin the existing `claude-opus-4-8: supports_temperature False` and `us./global.` rows were added to suppress.
scenarios: After the upgrade, every Opus 5.5 verifier call emits the temperature-reject warning the 4.8 rows suppressed
The new Bedrock 5.5 ids warm prompts against a 4096 cache minimum that is likely wrong (the 4.x Opus Bedrock measurement was lower), re-opening defect e3cd for the new family
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach step 2, after the audit, add an explicit sub-task: for each new 5.5 id, write the measured `supports_temperature`/`native_output_with_thinking` row into `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` and a cache-minimum into `_MODEL_CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS`, mirroring the existing 4.x rows.

evidence: .github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml:3-5 — 'Only inference-profile IDs (us. or global.) are invokable, and their suffixes are not uniform. Copy new IDs verbatim from aws bedrock list-inference-profiles --region <region>.'

capabilities.py:246-247 — '# Bedrock requires the dated Haiku profile id. The bare alias fails request validation.' This is a CONTRADICTED signal for the plan's bare 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5'.
The plan states Bedrock 'now serves' the three bare ids but cites no observed `list-inference-profiles` output confirming the exact 5.5 profile suffixes.

findings.location: Context/Problem paragraph 2; Approach step 2 (model upgrade); AC line 'rebar.toml, .github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml and MODEL_WINDOW_LADDER name Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5'
scenarios: Pinning the bare Haiku 5.5 id and having every trivial-class LLM op fail request validation at runtime after ship.
Opus/Sonnet 5.5 bare ids resolving to a non-invokable alias so the model upgrade silently fails over to the Anthropic fallback (or fails closed) only when exercised live.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture `aws bedrock list-inference-profiles --region us-east-1` output for the three 5.5 families in the ADR, and pin the verbatim profile ids (not bare family names); add any dated-id capability-override rows mirroring the existing Haiku 4.5 entry if the 5.5 profiles are versioned.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the ADR's model-call audit, record each 5.5 API-behavior claim with its evidence class (Verified via an observed test request / Unverified) and confirm the always-on-thinking + PromptedOutput structured path on a live Opus 5.5 call before relying on it.
evidence: Approach step 2 lists five concrete 5.5 behaviors as asserted facts with no source: 'forced tool_choice any/tool returns a 400 on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5', 'thinking can't be disabled on Opus 5.5', 'temperature, top_p and top_k are rejected', 'assistant prefill is rejected', 'Opus 5.5's effort defaults to medium'.

Approach step 3's safety claim that the rejection of forced tool_choice 'cannot reach' rebar and that 'prompted output works with Opus 5.5's always-on thinking' is load-bearing on the always-on-thinking assertion being correct.

The rubric's EMPIRICISM DEPTH requires classifying each such signal into an evidence class and warns: 'Do NOT mark a signal verified on general knowledge alone' — the plan records none of these as Verified vs Unverified.
findings.finding: The plan's Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 API-change assertions (forced tool_choice returns 400, thinking cannot be disabled, temperature/top_p/top_k rejected, prefill rejected, effort defaults to medium) are stated as established facts without a recorded evidence class or observed probe, yet the structured-output safety argument and the audit depend on them being true.
findings.location: Approach step 2 (model-call audit bullets) and step 3 ('prompted output works with Opus 5.5's always-on thinking')
scenarios: An assumed 5.5 behavior (e.g. effort default, or always-on thinking interacting with PromptedOutput) differing from reality, so the structured-output path the plan relies on misbehaves only under the new model.
The audit being treated as a confirmation step for claims already assumed true, rather than a probe that could falsify the plan's output-mode safety argument.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short observed-probe step (one structured call each on Opus/Sonnet 5.5) to the audit, and in the ADR label every 5.5 behavior assertion Verified/Unverified/Contradicted rather than stating them as settled facts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the ADR/plan how each agentic severity (blocker/major/minor/trivial) maps onto the sidecar finding's `decision` value and its priority/validity/impact/block_threshold/blocking_enabled fields that recall, norm_id and sign-review read.
evidence: passes.py:7: 'NO severity, NO confidence' — the current finder emits no severity; severity+decision are computed downstream
decide_ops.py:176 and orchestrator.py:258/271 set `decision`/`severity`/`priority`/`validity`/`impact` in Pass-2/3

sidecar.py build_payload._slim persists decision, severity, validity, impact, priority, block_threshold, blocking_enabled per finding; sidecar.surfaced_findings filters on decision in ('block','advisory') and prior_concerns recall reads float(priority)
Plan: 'Map agentic findings onto the existing verdict and sidecar schema, so downstream readers need no change' — names the obligation without specifying the field-level mapping
findings.finding: The agentic finding severity enum (blocker/major/minor/trivial) is defined with a severity->verdict rule, but the plan never specifies how that enum maps onto the existing sidecar's `decision` vocabulary (block/advisory/dropped/indeterminate/overflow) and its numeric fields (priority, validity, impact, block_threshold, blocking_enabled) that the current pipeline's Pass-2/Pass-3 compute and sidecar._slim persists. The agentic engine has no verify/decide pass to produce those fields.
findings.location: Approach step 4 (Verdict adapter); Goal 2 / Invariant 'Same surfaces'
scenarios: A `major` agentic finding: does it write decision='advisory', and what priority/block_threshold does sidecar/recall see?
A remediation re-review's prior_concerns recall (sidecar.py:422) reads float(priority) and block_threshold from an agentic-produced sidecar — undefined values break recall/decision_margin

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the `engine` provenance value vocabulary (the exact identifier for the 4-pass pipeline and for the agentic engine) recorded on the attestation and sidecar coverage.
evidence: Plan: 'The attestation records which engine produced it' and coverage 'records `engine` and the failure class'
Plan: comparison harness 'report verdict agreement' per engine and the production AC records 'Verdict, engine and attestation'
No section enumerates the `engine` field's permitted values; attest.py/sidecar.py carry no existing `engine` key to inherit one from
findings.finding: The attestation and sidecar coverage are required to record WHICH engine produced the verdict (Invariant 'Same certification', Fail-closed 'records engine'), and the comparison harness and production AC read it, but the plan never defines the value vocabulary of the `engine` field (the identifier strings for the 4-pass pipeline vs. the single-agent agentic engine).
findings.location: Invariants 'Same certification' / 'Fail closed'; Approach step 5 (Comparison harness); AC 'engine recorded'
scenarios: The comparison harness and the engine-provenance tests must agree on the exact engine identifier strings to assert equality
A sidecar/attestation consumer filtering by engine needs the canonical value set

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `.github/llm-providers/anthropic.toml` to the model-upgrade inventory and move its `[llm] model` and all three class slots to the 5.5 families alongside `rebar.toml` and `bedrock.toml`.
evidence: Plan: “Move `[llm] model` and the `frontier` / `standard` / `trivial` classes, with their Anthropic fallbacks, to Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, in both `rebar.toml` and `.github/llm-providers/bedrock.toml`.”

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `config.DEFAULT_MODEL`, `config.VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` and `model_classes.TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL` to the model-upgrade inventory and move each to its 5.5 family.
evidence: Plan: “Update `model_classes.MODEL_WINDOW_LADDER`, and the `sizing.py` family ladder if it needs it.” — names ladders but no default-model constant.
`config.py:61` `DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-opus-4-8"`; `config.py:67` `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-4-6"`.

`model_classes.py:45` `TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-haiku-4-5"`; `model_classes.py:53-56` `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS` wires these three as the class defaults, and the module docstring states the built-in defaults “reproduce today's model choices exactly.”
findings.finding: The model-upgrade inventory names `MODEL_WINDOW_LADDER` and the `sizing.py` ladder but omits the built-in default model constants `DEFAULT_MODEL` (`config.py:61` = `claude-opus-4-8`), `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` (`config.py:67` = `claude-sonnet-4-6`) and `TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL` (`model_classes.py:45` = `claude-haiku-4-5`) — the symbols that hold 'every configured model' when no config table overrides them.
findings.location: Approach §2 (Model upgrade) and Goal 3 (“Upgrade every configured model to the latest model in its family”)
scenarios: `config.py` `DEFAULT_MODEL` / `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` and `model_classes.py` `TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL` — any checkout or op that resolves models without a provider-overlay config (defaults path) keeps running Opus/Sonnet/Haiku 4.x after the upgrade, so 'every configured model' is not met and the default-path verifier still selects a 4.x model.
findings.suggested_fix: Run `find_referencing_symbols` on `DEFAULT_MODEL`/`VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL`/`TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL` and grep the three family strings across `src/rebar/llm/` so the upgrade also updates the default-holding constants, not just the config files and window ladder.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Divide plan-review-gate.md / config.md ownership between 0376 (surface parameters) and 2886 (config key + precedence) so the engine switch is documented once, consistently.
evidence: Child 0376 Scope: 'docs/mcp-reference.md, docs/plan-review-gate.md'.

Child 2886 Scope: 'docs/config.md (key documented)' — note 2886 documents the switch in config.md, but the plan-review-gate doc describing the engine selection is not disambiguated from 0376's surface documentation; both touch the plan-review gate docs surface and the engine switch it exposes.
findings.finding: Scope overlap on docs/plan-review-gate.md: two siblings list the same documentation file in their Scope without a stated division of which engine/surface content each owns, risking conflicting edits to one file.
scenarios: 0376 documents the --engine flag / MCP parameter in docs/plan-review-gate.md while 2886 documents the [verify] plan_review_engine key, and the two land conflicting descriptions of the same selection mechanism in the gate doc.
findings.suggested_fix: State in 0376 and 2886 which file/section each owns (0376: CLI/MCP parameter reference; 2886: config key semantics and precedence), cross-referencing rather than duplicating.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the hard landing order (2886 → 2473, with 75af before/with 2473) as explicit dependencies so the raise is only removed once the agentic step and verdict adapter exist.
evidence: Child 2886: 'Because this lands before the agentic engine exists, `"agentic"` passes validation but `review_plan` raises a config error ... the agentic-engine ticket that follows replaces that raise with its workflow step.'

Child 2473: 'src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py (remove the not-yet-available raise)' and adds the `agentic_review` step 'replacing the not-yet-available raise the engine-switch ticket left [rebar:skilled-cepevorous-naga]'.
Neither child's acceptance criteria encode the before/after ordering as a dependency; the roster shows no explicit dep edge for this sequencing.
findings.finding: Ordering/dependency wiring for the plan-review.yaml workflow and the 'not-yet-available raise' is asserted across three children (2886 adds the raise + `engine=='pipeline'` condition; 2473 removes the raise + adds the `agentic_review` step; 75af routes the adapted verdict through the post-dispatch path) but no child states the landing order as a hard dependency, so a reordered merge leaves either a half-wired agentic path (raise removed before the step/adapter exist) or a permanently unreachable agentic branch.
scenarios: 2473 merges before 2886: the raise it tries to remove does not yet exist, and `engine=='agentic'` has no guard, exposing a half-wired path.
2473's workflow step and 75af's adapter land in different order, so `agentic_review` runs but the verdict adapter is absent (or vice versa).
findings.suggested_fix: Add dependency edges: 2473 depends on 2886 (raise exists to remove) and on 75af (adapter exists to consume the agentic findings) before the `agentic_review` step is reachable.

evidence: Approach step 1 records 'the severity-to-verdict mapping (DECIDED 2026-11-09: only `blocker` blocks; `major`, `minor` and `trivial` are advisory)'
Invariant 'Fail closed': 'Only a clean, completed run with zero `blocker` findings is a PASS.'

AC5 pins only the schema shape (BLOCK | PASS | INDETERMINATE, `blocking`, `advisory`) and AC6 pins non-blocking PASS, but neither asserts that a `major`/`minor`/`trivial` finding yields a non-blocking verdict while a `blocker` yields BLOCK under the agentic engine
ABSENCE: no AC maps agentic finding severities to the blocking/advisory partition
